## Goal

Make it impossible for sample or test data, or for test cleanup, to reach or weaken the production record.

## Context

The fixture commands choose their target database from ambient configuration with no positive confirmation of what they are pointing at, their cleanup runs as several separate statements and changes the state of table-level protections while it runs, and an interrupted run can leave those protections inactive. A database test teardown uses a similar pattern. Details are in the owner's private tracker.

## Scope

- A positive target check for every fixture and test command: they run only against a database that identifies itself as disposable.
- End the lifecycle of the whole test database instead of weakening table protections, and make any remaining protection change atomic and self-restoring.
- Separate the migration owner from the application role, and document which role each command uses.
- Exclude test records from public projections.
- `docs/TESTING.md` and `docs/DATABASE.md` updated.

## Out of scope

- Changing what the fixtures contain, beyond what the exclusion needs.
- Changing production migrations.
- Excluding fixture records from public outputs, statistics and exports. That is SC-024 (#29), a public-launch blocker, and this issue stays open until its criterion is met.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixture command refuses a database that is not marked disposable, proven by a test.
- [ ] After an interrupted cleanup, every protection is active again, proven by a test.
- [ ] A full run of the database suite leaves every protection enabled, checked and reported.
- [ ] Public projections contain no test record. Owned by SC-024 (#29); this issue closes only when that criterion is verified.

## Required tests

- DB tests for the target check and for the interrupted cleanup.
- `pnpm test:db` before and after, with the real summary lines.
- All standard checks.

## Dependencies

- SC-003

P1 · Phase A
